limitations: The benchmark uses automated scoring of consistency with supplied documents; it does not establish an error rate across everyday use or factual question answering.

statement.document_title: Sam Altman Is Full Of Shit

from_speaker: a machine that continually gets things wrong
our_interpretation: I assess the embedded factual assertion about generative AI errors, not the surrounding advice about what readers should embrace.
The plain reading of continually is recurring factual mistakes across repeated use, not that every answer is wrong.
The relevant systems are contemporary general-purpose generative language models. No numerical error rate or claim of inevitable future failure is supplied.
For this ongoing state, I use April 2024, the latest complete calendar month before the May 21 post, as the reporting snapshot. These models have no standardized quarterly reporting period.
Errors include unsupported factual additions when summarizing supplied material and false answers to factual questions. These tasks must not be treated as having interchangeable error rates.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations document recurring factual errors across several widely used generative models, using repeated tests rather than a single anecdote.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, reproducible evaluations show that factual errors are absent or confined to isolated exceptions across representative tasks and contemporary systems.
